extDescription: Let your own AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or any MCP client) use this Firefox, with your tabs and logins. Runs on your computer. Needs a small helper app.
needUpdateIntro: Your helper app (v$1) is too old for this add-on (v$2). Run this again:
softUpdateIntro: Helper v$1 works, but v$2 is out. To update, run this again:
openPowerShell: Open PowerShell (Start menu → type “powershell” → Enter) and paste:
openTerminalMac: Open Terminal (⌘ Space → type “terminal” → Enter) and paste:
manualWin: Or download the app and double-click it (if SmartScreen warns: More info → Run anyway).
manualUnix: Or download the app, then run: $1
updatesItself: This page updates by itself once it’s installed.
copyFailed: Copy failed: select the text and press Ctrl+C
hintClaudeApp: Add this to claude_desktop_config.json (Claude app → Settings → Developer → Edit Config), then restart the Claude app. Needs Node.js.
hintRunIn: Run this in $1. It replaces any “firefox” server $2 already has.
hintCodex: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml, replacing any [mcp_servers.firefox] section already there.
hintCodexWsl: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml inside WSL, replacing any [mcp_servers.firefox] section already there.
hintOpencode: Merge this into opencode.json (in your project, or in ~/.config/opencode/).
hintOpencodeWsl: Merge this into opencode.json inside WSL (in your project, or in ~/.config/opencode/).
hintOther: Add this to your client’s MCP config file, next to any servers already there.
hintOtherWsl: Add this to your client’s MCP config file inside WSL, next to any servers already there.
wslAddrChanges: The Windows address in it changes when Windows restarts: copy this again if your AI stops connecting.
wslReplaceIp: Replace WINDOWS-IP with the output of: $1
firewallNote: The first time, Windows may ask to let foxhand-host through the firewall: tick Private networks and click Allow.
askBeforeClosing: Require confirm for closing and deleting
nothingYet: Nothing yet. Once your AI sends a command, it shows up here.
newTokenNote: A new token locks out every AI using the old one until you copy the config again.
bindNote: 127.0.0.1 = this computer only. 0.0.0.0 = your whole network, protected only by the token.
wslOff: Off: AIs in WSL can’t reach Firefox until you turn this on.
wslNoAdapter: No WSL network adapter found. Is WSL running?
reloadHint: Reload this page. If it keeps happening, restart Firefox.
newTokenActive: New token active. Copy the config into your AI again.
savedPort: Saved. Copy the config into your AI again if the port changed.
errPort: Port must be a number between 1024 and 65535
errBind: Listen on must be an IP address like 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0
evHelperUpdated: Helper updated to v$1, restarting it
evNoAnswer: Helper didn’t answer within $1 s; starting it again
errHelperOld: Helper app v$1 is too old for this add-on. Run the install command again.
errAddonOld: This add-on is older than the helper app (v$1). Update the add-on.
hintPaused: Every AI command is refused until you resume.
hintReady: Your AI can use this Firefox. Pause any time.
hintReadyIdle: Helper running. Copy the MCP config and add it to your AI tool to connect.
hintReadyUpdate: Your AI can use this Firefox. A newer helper is available; update when it suits you.
hintNoHelper: Foxhand needs a small helper app to talk to your AI. Install it with the command below.
hintHelperOld: The helper app is too old for this add-on. Run the command below to update it.
hintAddonOld: This add-on is older than the helper app. Update Foxhand from Firefox’s Add-ons page.
hintPort: Another program may be using the port. Change it in Settings → Token and port.
hintNotRunning: Firefox can’t reach the helper app. Press Retry, or open Settings for details.
nowEmpty: Nothing yet. Ask your AI to do something in Firefox.
connectLead: Pick your AI tool, copy the config, then run or paste it where your AI reads its MCP settings. This page shows when the first command arrives.
configSecret: This config contains your access token. Treat it like a password: anyone who has it can control this Firefox. Don’t paste it into chats, issues or screenshots.
connDone: Your AI is connected: $1 commands so far.
connNeedsHelper: Waiting for the helper app. Check the status above.
safetyLead: These apply while your AI is working. Pausing is the only control that stops everything.
pauseRowNote: Press this shortcut, or use Pause AI in the toolbar popup. Every command is refused until you resume. To change the shortcut, open Firefox’s Add-ons page and choose Manage Extension Shortcuts.
showCursorNote: A cursor and an orange bubble show where the AI is acting and why. It never blocks your own mouse or keyboard.
guardNote: Closing tabs and windows and deleting bookmarks or cookies are refused unless the AI passes confirm:true. This catches accidents, but the AI sets it itself, so it isn’t an approval prompt for you.
passwordsNote: No tool reads Firefox’s saved logins or password manager. The AI can still see and act on any page you’re signed in to.
activityLead: What your AI did recently. Cleared when Firefox restarts.
advancedLead: Helper details, access token, port and uninstall. You rarely need these.
annNote: Shown once, from foxhand.pages.dev. Links open in a new tab.
obHelp1: Foxhand only works while Firefox is open.
obHelp2: Make sure step 1 says the helper is running, then copy the config again. A changed token or port needs a fresh copy.
obHelp3: Start a new session in your AI tool after adding the config. Many tools only read their MCP settings when they start.
obIntro: Foxhand lets your AI agent use this Firefox, with your tabs and your logins, through MCP. Everything stays on your computer. Setup takes about a minute.
obRenamed: WebMCP Controller is now called Foxhand. Same add-on, same settings. If step 1 asks, run the install command once more to update the helper.
ob1Why: Firefox add-ons can’t open network ports, so a small helper app serves MCP for Foxhand. It only listens on this computer.
ob2Waiting: Waiting for your AI’s first command…
obWslNote: AI running inside WSL? Set that up in Settings → Connect your AI.
obTry1: Look at my open tabs and group them by topic.
obTry2: Open github.com/hamb1y/foxhand and tell me what changed in the latest release.
obTry3: Search my history for the last article I read about Firefox and summarize it.
obTipCursor: A cursor shows where the AI is acting, with an orange bubble saying what it’s doing.
obTipPause: Press $1 (or Pause AI in the toolbar popup) to stop every command at once.
obTipSafety: Closing tabs and deleting bookmarks or cookies need confirm:true from the AI. That guards against mistakes; it isn’t a pop-up asking you. Pause is the real stop button. No tool reads Firefox’s saved passwords.
